findings.sourceEvidence: "Deleveraging Trigger Period" means any period (other than a Second Deleveraging Trigger Period, determined without regard to clause (ii) of the definition thereof) after the Original Effective Date from and including the first Business Day to occur on or after any day on which the Administrative Agent determines that the Prevailing Market Value of the Collateral as at 9:00 am (Eastern Time) on that day and the immediately preceding day is less than 70% of the Initial Prevailing Market Value to but excluding the first Business Day thereafter to occur on or after any day on which the Administrative Agent determines that the Prevailing Market Value of the Collateral as at 9:00 am (Eastern Time) on that day and the immediately preceding day is equal to or greater than the Initial Prevailing Market Value.
findings.proposedIrEvidence: calculationExpression: {kind: COMPARE, left: METRIC_REFERENCE(Prevailing Market Value of the Collateral), operator: LT, right: MULTIPLY(0.7, Initial Prevailing Market Value)} - presented as a computed (non-UNSUPPORTED) node despite sufficiency=PARTIAL
findings.verifierReasoning: The source defines a stateful, hysteretic *period* with distinct entry (PMV < 70% of Initial, on two consecutive days) and exit (PMV >= 100% of Initial, on two consecutive days) thresholds, an explicit mutual-exclusivity carve-out from Second Deleveraging Trigger Period, and Business-Day snapping. The proposed IR reduces this to a single stateless COMPARE testing only the 70% entry threshold, with no exit-threshold logic, no two-day persistence test, no Business Day snap, and no exclusion for periods that are simultaneously a Second Deleveraging Trigger Period. This produces different real-world answers than the source: e.g., if PMV drops to 60% of Initial (entering a Deleveraging Trigger Period) and later recovers to 80% of Initial (still below the 100% exit threshold), the source says the Deleveraging Trigger Period is still ongoing, but the IR's COMPARE (80% < 70%? = false) would say it has ended. Likewise, when PMV falls below 50% of Initial (a Second Deleveraging Trigger Period), the IR's Deleveraging Trigger Period COMPARE would also evaluate true (50% < 70%), contrary to the source's explicit carve-out that a Second Deleveraging Trigger Period is not also a Deleveraging Trigger Period. Since Fixed Rate, the LTV Table selection, and other economics keyed to 'which regime is in effect' depend on this determination, this is a real, exploitable discrepancy, not merely an honest disclosure - the node is not marked UNSUPPORTED (unlike sibling terms such as Initial LTV/Liquidation LTV, which do flag the identical regime-selection problem as UNSUPPORTED).

findings.sourceEvidence: "Second Deleveraging Trigger Period" means any period after the Original Effective Date from and including the first Business Day to occur on or after any day on which the Administrative Agent determines that the Prevailing Market Value of the Collateral as at 9:00 am (Eastern Time) on that day and the immediately preceding day is less than 50% of the Initial Prevailing Market Value to but excluding the first Business Day to occur on or after any day when the Administrative Agent determines that (i) the Prevailing Market Value of the Collateral as at 9:00 am (Eastern Time) on that day and the immediately preceding day is equal to or greater than the Initial Prevailing Market Value or (ii) a Deleveraging Trigger Period is in effect.
findings.proposedIrEvidence: calculationExpression: {kind: COMPARE, left: METRIC_REFERENCE(Prevailing Market Value of the Collateral), operator: LT, right: MULTIPLY(0.5, Initial Prevailing Market Value)} - presented as a computed node despite sufficiency=PARTIAL, with no representation of either exit branch (i) or (ii)
findings.verifierReasoning: As with Deleveraging Trigger Period, the source defines this as a hysteretic period with a distinct exit condition that fires on EITHER full recovery to 100% of Initial OR the onset of a (lesser) Deleveraging Trigger Period, plus a two-consecutive-day persistence test and Business Day snapping. The IR collapses this to a bare point-in-time comparison against only the 50% entry threshold, omitting both exit branches entirely. This means the IR would classify the period as ended the moment PMV crosses back above 50% of Initial, whereas the source keeps the Second Deleveraging Trigger Period in effect until PMV fully recovers to 100% of Initial (or, per clause (ii), technically never exits into 'no trigger period' status without first exiting into a Deleveraging Trigger Period). This produces materially different capacity/rate/LTV conclusions than the source in the same recovery scenario as flagged for the sibling term.

findings.verifierReasoning: The Blocking Event definition has five independently-operative clauses (a)-(e). The dependsOnTerms list captures terms relevant to clauses (a), (d) and (e) but includes nothing corresponding to clauses (b) (Loan acceleration/repayment under Section 2.03) or (c) (Lender notice of a Section 2.07 event) - e.g. no 'Loan' term dependency and no cross-reference marker for Section 2.07. The overall calculationExpression is already honestly flagged UNSUPPORTED/PARTIAL, which limits reliance on the computed logic, but the dependsOnTerms metadata itself is silently incomplete in a way that could mislead a downstream consumer about which definitions/sections actually feed this term, independent of the acknowledged computation gap.
